about: The priest signs himself and begins the Mass with In nómine Patris. The antiphon “Introíbo ad altáre Dei” comes from Ps 42:4 in the Vulgate (Ps 43:4 in Hebrew numbering). It precedes the psalm from which it is taken and is repeated after the psalm ends.

seg.nr: The vested priest approaches the altar, makes the reverence due to it, signs himself from forehead to breast and says aloud:

seg.tr: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

ex.w007: “Spíritus” can be nominative or genitive. The following “Sancti” (w008) establishes the genitive here: “of the Holy Ghost”.

seg.nr: With hands joined before his breast, the priest begins the antiphon.

seg.tr: I will go to the altar of God.
To God, who gladdens my youth.

ex.w018: The Latin “youth” corresponds to the Greek text of the psalm. The Hebrew text speaks here of joy.
